analysis.title: US TMT Today - 4 Nov 2026
key_insights: NDX futures rallied about 400 bps from the overnight lows. NDX outperformed Semis (SOX) by nearly 460 bps on the day, a top-10 daily spread in 10+ years. Semis moved further below their 200-day moving average, with INTC, CBRS, MRVL, TER, CAT and FFIV described as oversold.

Investor conversations focus on the magnitude of the moves more than their direction, including whether the market may over-price potential policy outcomes if the moves continue past today. Examples cited: cloud service providers (CSPs) outperforming Semis, drawdowns in IPPs or E&Cs, and a sharp rally in consumer discretionary.

With earnings, AI datapoints and conference season fading, attention shifts to policy narratives through the end of 2026. Oil is at 1-month lows and 30-year and 10-year yields are back to mid-September levels. GS Economics expects data center moratoria to fade in importance and not be long-lived if enacted, since data centers are low on voters' priority list.

Top investor inbounds: why AMZN is outperforming by so much, why broad Internet is rallying (EXPE, DASH, APP), Apple back at all-time highs, nuance in Semis/AI infra (FLEX down 14%), earnings move magnitude (DUOL, YOU, BKNG), and DDOG read-through to consumption.

AMD was flat after being +9% the prior night. The note sees no earnings-related reason for the fade: AMD addressed the two main concerns, 2027 gross margins (GS raised its '27 GM estimate to 55.7%) and 4Q/2027 revenue amid PC headwinds (offset by data center strength, with AMD guiding to >80% revenue growth in '27). The debate likely shifts to the multiple as GPUs mix in and Semis de-rate, and to industry execution on GW build-outs. GS GIR sits at about $27.35 in '28.

ANET was +5% after being +10% the prior night. The note calls it possibly one of the better prints of this AI cycle: revenue accelerated into the 50s y/y and CY'27 started at +38-40% y/y against a ~30% expectation. Nitpicks are the q/q decline in deferred revenue (DR) and decelerating bookings growth, which the note says investors are largely ignoring. GS GIR now sits slightly below ~$8 non-GAAP EPS in '28.
More than 30 TMT companies report after the close on 4 Nov, including AMC, APP, ARM, COHR, EXPE, HUBS, MELI, MSI, QCOM, SNAP, TKO, ZG and WOLF. FWONK, SPHR and Unity report pre-market on 5 Nov.

Semiconductor forward multiples compressed more than 40% over two months, from 28x to 16x. The SOX's roughly 2x forward P/E discount to the S&P 500 is near the widest in 15 years. The note frames the next debate as what was priced in.
US Internet vs S&P 500 is charted against inverted oil/crude, which the note says explains part of the day's move.

BKNG rose 11%, one of its largest one-day moves in 10+ years. The note cites positioning (~20mn shares short per Bloomberg), valuation (15+ year low in forward EV/EBITDA going into the print), and a perceived 'last cut' dynamic from +1-3% room night (RN) guidance for 4Q, given the oil and rates move. Consensus still sits at high-single-digit y/y growth in RNs and gross bookings (GBs) for '27.

Brent is having one of its biggest 5-day declines in recent history, down about $18 net over five days. This produced a roughly 15-point spread between Energy and Consumer Discretionary GICS sectors over the last 5 sessions.
MSFT registered a new all-time high, a turnaround from the narrative overhang the stock faced through much of 2H'25 and 1H'26.

ANET (reported 11/3 after close): revenue growth accelerated into the 50s y/y. CY'27 started at +38-40% y/y revenue growth against a ~30% expectation going into the print. The q/q decline in deferred revenue and the slowdown in bookings growth were the only pushbacks. GS GIR non-GAAP EPS for '28 is slightly below ~$8.
BKNG: stock +11% after earnings. 4Q room night guidance of +1-3%. Consensus for '27 is high-single-digit y/y growth in room nights and gross bookings.

Earnings after the close on 11/4 (30+ TMT names): AMC, AMPL, APP, ARM, CGNX, CHYM, COHR, CPAY, CRUS, DDD, EXPE, FICO, FIG, FSLY, GTM, HUBS, KVYO, LUMN, MELI, MGNI, MKSI, MSI, PAYC, POWI, PTC, PTRN, QCOM, RPD, SBGI, SNAP, SEZL, TKO, VECO, VERX, VIAV, WU, WOLF, ZG.
